solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Second date broken by youth leader's girlfriend

indicators.note: something broken is smashed apart, so the letters of date are rearranged
the leader of a word is its opening letter, so youth gives only its first

explanation.surface: A man's date falls through because a youth club leader's girlfriend gets in the way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broken' rearranges the letters of date. 'girlfriend' is the definition: a steady is a regular partner.
explanation.definitionFit: A steady is a regular romantic partner, someone you have been going out with for a while.

clue.text: Impertinence one might get from a waiter

definitions.meaning: cheek or insolence, as in 'none of your lip'

definitions.text: one might get from a waiter
definitions.meaning: a waiter brings condiments such as ketchup or gravy to the table

explanation.walkthrough: Two readings: cheek, and a relish served with a meal.
explanation.definitionFit: Cheek is called this informally, and the same word is a liquid relish brought with food.

clue.text: Has a picnic — or goes to a restaurant

definitions.meaning: taken literally, dines in the open air
the usual idiom for dining away from home

explanation.walkthrough: The first reading is the literal one: eating outdoors. 'or' just joins the two.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase literally means dining outdoors, and idiomatically means dining at a restaurant rather than at home.

clue.text: Curse the motherland

parts.note: read as an oath against one's country: a swear word followed by the word for a people's homeland, run together

explanation.walkthrough: The clue splits into a swear word and a word for a country, which merge, sharing their N, into the oath.
explanation.definitionFit: Eternal condemnation, also used as an oath or curse, fitting a curse uttered against a country.

clue.text: Frenchwoman forced to take in a Frenchman

indicators.note: one piece takes in another by enclosing it

parts.note: to be forced is to be made to do something
M is the abbreviation for monsieur, a French man

explanation.surface: A Frenchwoman is compelled to give a Frenchman a bed for the night.
explanation.walkthrough: M for monsieur is a standard abbreviation; A and M sit inside MADE.
explanation.definitionFit: The French title for a married woman, used in English for a Frenchwoman.

clue.text: Turkish leader elected once more

parts.note: an aga was a military commander or chief in the Ottoman empire
a politician who is elected is in office

explanation.surface: The Turkish head of state is returned to power for another term.
explanation.walkthrough: AGA is an Ottoman title; IN as 'elected', as in 'the party got in'.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: something done once more is done a second time.

clue.text: Man devoured by a lion, perhaps — a circus performer

indicators.note: something devoured ends up inside the eater, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: a lion is an example of a big cat
Rob is a man's name

explanation.surface: In the circus, a performer is eaten by a lion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'devoured by' puts the man inside the big cat. 'lion, perhaps' signals an example, not a lion itself.
explanation.definitionFit: A tumbler or trapeze artist who performs gymnastic feats under the big top.

clue.text: Always on the go, is Ivy!

parts.note: ever means always, as in 'ever hopeful'
a green light means go

explanation.surface: Someone remarks that a woman called Ivy never stops moving.
explanation.walkthrough: Ivy reads as a woman's name but is the plant. GREEN comes from traffic lights, where green means go.
explanation.definitionFit: Ivy keeps its leaves all year round, an example of a plant that never goes bare.

clue.text: The point at which the tourist's declared?

definitions.text: The point at which the tourist's declared?

parts.words: The point at which the tourist's declared?
parts.note: travellers must declare dutiable goods at a border checkpoint; the surface pretends the tourist is being announced

explanation.walkthrough: 'declared' suggests a proclamation, but it is the declaration of goods to officials at a frontier.
explanation.definitionFit: The checkpoint at a port or airport where arriving travellers state any dutiable goods.

clue.text: See 8
No beer left? That's the limit!

definitions.text: No beer left? That's the limit!

parts.words: No beer left? That's the limit!
parts.note: the last of a pint of ale reaches its final drop, and the phrase means the very last extremity

explanation.walkthrough: Bitter is a British pale ale; its end is the last of it, and the phrase means holding out to the very last.
explanation.definitionFit: To the very last extremity, however unpleasant: the furthest limit of endurance.

clue.text: Flags put out in honour of a brave man

definitions.meaning: bunting and flags hung up for a festival

definitions.text: in honour of a brave man

explanation.walkthrough: Two senses: festive bunting, and a medal pinned on a hero.
explanation.definitionFit: Ornament hung up for a celebration, and an award such as a medal given for valour.

clue.text: Childishly claims the luggage

definitions.meaning: children shout this word to stake a claim, as in 'I call first go'

explanation.walkthrough: British children claim something by calling out the word: 'Bags I the front seat!'
explanation.definitionFit: Schoolyard slang for staking a claim, and a plural noun for cases carried when travelling.

clue.text: All the players express mild disapproval before taking it back

indicators.note: one piece comes before the other in the answer

parts.note: tut is the clicking sound of mild reproach

indicators.note: taken back means read in reverse, so the word it is turned round

explanation.surface: Every performer tuts at something before withdrawing it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns it round; 'tut' is the reproving click of the tongue. The definition is a musical term from Italian.
explanation.definitionFit: A musical direction meaning everyone in the orchestra plays together.

clue.text: Where men with convictions took steps to create revolution

definitions.text: Where men with convictions took steps to create revolution

parts.words: Where men with convictions took steps to create revolution
parts.note: Victorian prisoners were made to climb steps on a turning wheel; convictions and revolution suggest political rebels

explanation.walkthrough: 'men with convictions' reads as idealists and 'revolution' as an uprising, but they are convicts turning a wheel.
explanation.definitionFit: A penal wheel turned by prisoners stepping on it, now any wearisome routine.

clue.text: Hire-tent collapsing? Unlucky for some

indicators.note: a tent collapsing falls into a jumble, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A rented marquee falls down, which is bad luck for the guests.
explanation.walkthrough: 'collapsing' rearranges the letters of Hire-tent. 'Unlucky for some' is the bingo call for this number.
explanation.definitionFit: The number held to bring bad luck, the traditional bingo caller's phrase for it.

clue.text: Trumped in error — that's indiscreet

indicators.note: letters in error are wrongly placed, so they need rearranging

explanation.surface: A card player trumps a trick by mistake, a rash move.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' belongs to the fodder; 'error' alone rearranges TRUMPED IN.
explanation.definitionFit: Unwise or rash; lacking caution, near in sense to indiscreet.

clue.text: Couturier resigned in a tantrum

indicators.note: someone in a tantrum is thrown into disorder, so the letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: A fashion house head quits after throwing a fit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in a tantrum' rearranges RESIGNED.
explanation.definitionFit: A couturier is a fashion creator, someone who designs clothes.

clue.text: Duck and dive

explanation.walkthrough: Duck is the verb, to dunk, not the bird.
explanation.definitionFit: To plunge something or oneself completely into a liquid.

clue.text: It may hold up current supplies

definitions.text: It may hold up current supplies

parts.words: It may hold up current supplies
parts.note: 'hold up' suggests a robbery of goods, but it means carrying electric power lines aloft

explanation.walkthrough: 'current' is electric current, not 'present'; 'hold up' is to support, not to rob.
explanation.definitionFit: A tall steel tower carrying overhead electricity cables.

clue.text: Fired with real reform and no exaggeration

parts.note: a fire that has been lit has been fired

indicators.note: to reform is to shape again, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A boss sacked someone with genuine reform plans, and that's no overstatement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fired' suggests sacked but means set alight; 'reform' rearranges REAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Exact, word-for-word, without embellishment; a literal account involves no overstatement.

clue.text: A mother and father figure

parts.note: a dam is the mother of an animal, especially a horse

explanation.surface: Someone who is both a mother and a father to a child.
explanation.walkthrough: DAM is a female parent of livestock.
explanation.definitionFit: In the Bible, the first man and father of the human race.

clue.text: Thus Indian gets confused by the vernacular

indicators.note: letters that get confused are jumbled, so they form a new order

explanation.surface: An Indian person is muddled by the local dialect.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gets confused' rearranges THUS INDIAN.
explanation.definitionFit: A colloquial language of northern India, the everyday tongue rather than a formal one.

clue.text: Move south down shore to get to bay, perhaps

indicators.note: to move a letter is to shift it to another position in the word
in a down clue, down means lower in the word, further towards the end

explanation.surface: Walk southwards along the beach to reach the bay.
explanation.walkthrough: S leaves the front of SHORE and goes down one place. 'bay, perhaps' suggests a coastal inlet but is a reddish-brown horse.
explanation.definitionFit: A bay is a horse of reddish-brown colour, so it is an example of the animal.

clue.text: Hose in New York left running

parts.note: a machine that is running is on

explanation.surface: A New York woman's stockings have a ladder in them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'running' suggests a ladder in stockings but gives ON.
explanation.definitionFit: Stockings are often called nylons after the synthetic fibre they are made from.

clue.text: You may take work home from it

definitions.text: You may take work home from it

parts.words: You may take work home from it
parts.note: 'work' reads as office duties, but means a book, borrowed and taken home

explanation.walkthrough: 'work' means a literary work, not a job.
explanation.definitionFit: A building where books can be borrowed and carried home to read.

clue.text: Play the fool? Sleep on it!

definitions.text: Play the fool? Sleep on it!

parts.words: Play the fool? Sleep on it!
parts.note: a roll of bedding to sleep on, with play on 'roll' as acting a part; the advice reads as 'think it over'

explanation.walkthrough: 'Sleep on it' looks like advice to wait; it is literal: one sleeps on this rolled bedding.
explanation.definitionFit: Bedding rolled up for carrying, spread out to sleep on when camping.

clue.text: Sound conductor of works by Schubert

indicators.note: sound means as heard spoken, so a word with the same pronunciation is wanted

parts.note: the conductor leads an orchestra, so is its leader

explanation.surface: A trustworthy conductor directs works by Schubert.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sound' looks like an adjective meaning reliable, but signals the homophone.
explanation.definitionFit: German art songs, of which Schubert wrote hundreds.

clue.text: Somehow lost on points — or was robbed?

indicators.note: somehow means in some way or other, so the letters are put in a different order

parts.note: E and N are points of the compass, east and north

explanation.surface: A boxer loses on points and feels cheated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' sets STOL (lost rearranged) on EN; 'was' joins the definition. 'points' suggests boxing scores but means compass points.
explanation.definitionFit: Taken unlawfully: goods robbed from a house have been taken by thieves.
